findings.description: _render_selector_codex renders only Codex Plan and Default payloads; it neither invokes the Claude renderer nor compares semantic payloads, so the selector_codex deterministic case cannot prove the claimed Claude-native/Codex semantic parity.
findings.suggestion: Render the Claude surface in this parity adapter and assert equality of the normalized semantic choice set, recommendation, and refusal choice across all three surfaces.

findings.description: The More/Back/Cancel/invalid checks call stateless continue_selector on freshly rendered dictionaries and never write, reload, or bound any continuation state, so they do not prove persisted loop pause/resume behavior despite the fixture contract claiming it.
findings.suggestion: Exercise the actual persisted continuation/pipeline-state path (including reload and bounded termination), or narrow the contract to the stateless continuation behavior that is actually tested.

summary_lines: FAIL: focused tests pass, but the deterministic adapter does not establish Claude-to-Codex semantic parity.
FAIL: continuation coverage is stateless and does not prove bounded persisted pause/resume.
PASS: Codex Plan selector, Codex Default fallback, overflow, cancel, and invalid-input rendering are exercised without claiming Codex clickability.
Verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_behavior.py tests/test_interaction.py tests/test_selector_contract.py (35 passed); .venv/bin/python -m renmark --behavior (6/6 passed).
